newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee dips as major bank resumes dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee dips as major bank resumes dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee saw some long-awaited movement on Thursday as a leading state-run bank resumed its normal dollar purchases after a 20-day break, dealers said.
This bank hit most Bombay banks, pushing the rupee to 35.89 level from the opening quote of 35.865/875, dealers said.
The bank, which buys dollars for leading state-run firms and influences the market, has not been active in the market for the past 20 days, dealers said.
The forward dollar market also saw a mild reversal of sentiment with corporates seeking cover, dealers said.
July dollars were quoted at 1.31/1.33 rupees at noon, up from the opening quote of 1.27/1.30 rupees, dealers said.
